Canonical main had no executable Kubernetes admission-policy artifact for either runtime boundary at rejoin.

identify ClayVerse Pods by canonical app label or clayverse container name, with previous-object identity retained across UPDATE
require exact kata-qemu-runtime-rs RuntimeClass for identified ClayVerse Pods

adversarial_review.counter_reality: A label-only policy could be weakened by an UPDATE that removes the label while introducing a dangerous runtime mutation, and static RuntimeClass presence in the repository template alone does not prevent later runtime-class drift.
adversarial_review.repair: Target identity now survives UPDATE through oldObject and is also recognized by the canonical clayverse container name; the same admission policy requires the exact reviewed RuntimeClass and rejects Kata runtime annotations.
adversarial_review.residual_uncertainty: A source YAML policy may still fail API admission, be absent/unbound on the target, or face a CREATE-time admission mutation that rewrites all ClayVerse identity markers before validation. Final effective-Pod identity and annotations must therefore be runtime-attested.

next_discriminator: On an authorized isolated Kubernetes/Kata-capable executor, apply the exact policy plus binding before the workload; prove clean ClayVerse Pod CREATE/UPDATE is admitted, wrong/missing RuntimeClass is denied, injected io.katacontainers.* annotations are denied, UPDATE identity-removal attempts remain fenced, and effective Pod identity/annotations are attested before continuing exact OCI/Kata/Tier-2 gates.
